proposals.before: When he traveled to Qi and heard the Shao music performed, for three months he was so enraptured that he could not taste his food.
proposals.after: When he traveled to Qi and heard the Shao music performed, for three months he was so enraptured that he did not notice the taste of meat.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 不知肉味 specifies meat flavor; idiomatic 'food' loses that concrete sense already preserved in the literal.

proposals.before: Chen She rose from the humblest origins, rallied a ragtag band of garrison conscripts, proclaimed himself king of Chu within a month, and was utterly destroyed in less than half a year — his enterprise could not have been more trifling. Yet the robed and belted scholars carried Confucius's ritual vessels to his court and pledged their service. Why?
proposals.after: Chen She rose from the humblest origins, rallied a ragtag band of garrison conscripts, proclaimed himself king of Chu within a month, and was utterly destroyed in less than half a year — his enterprise could not have been more trifling. Yet the robed and belted gentlemen-scholars carried Confucius's ritual vessels and went to pledge themselves as his subjects. Why?
proposals.reason: Chinese 往委質為臣者 denotes going to offer themselves as subjects/ministers; 'to his court and pledged their service' softens 委質為臣.

proposals.before: When the present emperor ascended the throne, men like Zhao Wan and Wang Zang, distinguished in Confucian learning, came to prominence, and the emperor himself was drawn to their tradition. He summoned men who were upright, worthy, and accomplished in the literary arts.
proposals.after: When the present emperor ascended the throne, men like Zhao Wan and Wang Zang were distinguished in Confucian learning, and the emperor himself was drawn to their tradition. He summoned men who were upright, worthy, and accomplished in the literary arts.
proposals.reason: Chinese 明儒學 characterizes their mastery of Confucian learning; it does not state that they came to prominence, which the idiomatic version invents.

proposals.before: When the present emperor ascended the throne, men such as Zhao Wan and Wang Zang, who were well versed in Confucian learning, came to prominence, and the emperor also inclined toward it; thereupon he recruited men who were upright, worthy, and accomplished in letters.
proposals.after: When the present emperor ascended the throne, men such as Zhao Wan and Wang Zang, who were well versed in Confucian learning, and the emperor also inclined toward it; thereupon he recruited men who were upright, worthy, and accomplished in letters.
proposals.reason: Same invention of came to prominence absent from 趙綰、王臧之屬明儒學; literal should not add that clause.

proposals.before: Wang Zang of Lanling, having studied the Odes under Master Shen, served Emperor Jing as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, but was later dismissed from the post.
proposals.after: Wang Zang of Lanling, having studied the Odes, served Emperor Jing as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, but was later dismissed from the post.
proposals.reason: Chinese 既受詩 only says Wang Zang had received instruction in the Odes; it does not name Master Shen in this unit. The idiomatic English invents that teacher attribution.

proposals.before: Yuan Gu said: "Master Gongsun, devote yourself to upright scholarship in your words, and do not twist your learning to flatter the age!"
proposals.after: Yuan Gu said: "Master Gongsun, devote yourself to upright scholarship so as to speak truly, and do not twist your learning to flatter the age!"
proposals.reason: 以言 marks purpose (speak from correct learning), not scholarship merely 'in your words'.

proposals.before: Once Er Kuan had mastered the Documents, he was recommended by his commandery on the basis of literary learning, went to study under the erudites, and received instruction from Kong Anguo.
proposals.after: After Er Kuan had mastered the Documents, he was recommended by his commandery on the basis of literary learning, went to study under the erudites, and received instruction from Kong Anguo.
proposals.reason: 'Once Er Kuan' is unnatural and creates a false capitalized span; 'After' matches 既.

proposals.before: Yan, along with the Xu family's disciples Gonghu Manyi, Master Huan, and Shan Ci, all served at one time as Grandees of the Han Ritual Office.
proposals.after: Yan, along with the Xu family's disciples Gonghu Manyi, Master Huan, and Shan Ci, all once served as Grandees of the Han Ritual Office.
proposals.reason: Chinese 皆嘗為 means each had at some point held the office, not that they held it simultaneously; 'at one time' is ambiguous.

proposals.before: Among Dong Zhongshu's most accomplished disciples were Chu Da of Lanling, Yin Zhong of Guangchuan, and Lu Bushu of Wen.
proposals.after: Among Dong Zhongshu's disciples who rose to success were Chu Da of Lanling, Yin Zhong of Guangchuan, and Lu Bushu of Wen.
proposals.reason: 遂者 means disciples who advanced or achieved success in office, not necessarily the most accomplished in learning; the literal already has 'who achieved success'.

decisions.reason: Focus unit 三月不知肉味 specifies meat (肉), not generic food; the proposed idiomatic restores that concrete sense already present in the literal.
往委質為臣者 means they went and offered themselves as subjects/ministers; 'to his court and pledged their service' softens 委質為臣, while the proposed wording restores going and becoming subjects.
趙綰、王臧之屬明儒學 only states that men of their sort were versed in Confucian learning; 'came to prominence' is not in the Chinese, and the proposed idiomatic removes that invention without harming grammar.

decisions.after: When the present emperor ascended the throne, men such as Zhao Wan and Wang Zang were well versed in Confucian learning, and the emperor also inclined toward it; thereupon he recruited men who were upright, worthy, and accomplished in letters.
decisions.reason: Removing invented 'came to prominence' is correct for 明儒學, but the proposed after leaves a verbless relative clause. Revising to 'were well versed in Confucian learning' keeps the correction and restores grammatical English.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 趙綰、王臧之屬明儒學，而上亦鄉之

decisions.reason: Although s0078 has only 既受詩, the preceding units describe Master Shen teaching the Odes and s0080 says Zhao Wan 亦嘗受詩申公, so 'also … under Master Shen' confirms Wang Zang's teacher. The idiomatic attribution is contextually accurate; stripping it is unnecessary pedantry.
務正學以言 uses 以言 as purpose/means—speak from upright learning—not 'scholarship in your words'; the proposed literal matches that construction and the idiomatic sense.
'Once Er Kuan had mastered…' is natural English for 既通尚書 and does not invent a capitalized name; changing Once to After is merely stylistic.
皆嘗為 means each had at some point held the office; 'at one time' can imply simultaneity, while 'all once served' matches 嘗 and the idiomatic 'at various times'.
弟子遂者 means disciples who succeeded or rose in career, as the following offices for Chu Da and Lu Bushu show; 'most accomplished' overreads scholarly excellence for 遂.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0003 shows 明儒學 only marks mastery of Confucian learning, not promotion or coming to prominence; revise role and action accordingly.
Same repair: Wang Zang is characterized by 明儒學, not by an invented rise to prominence; revise role and action to match.
